name: reporank
description: Ranks any repository out of 100 across eight weighted dimensions — documentation, structure, tests, code quality, security, activity, dependencies and mod-protocol conformance — and returns the concrete fixes that would raise the score, ordered by what each one is worth. Point it at a module name in the orbit, a local path, a GitHub repo or git URL (cloned on demand), or a localfs CID (restored on demand). Scoring is a modular panel of voters, one ballot per dimension per voter, in three kinds held in one registry: deterministic static scorers that read the collected evidence and need no model or key, agent voters that run on the claude agent (the agent module) and read the evidence and the code, and Agent Protocol v1 voters that hand the brief to an external agent and mine the ballot out of its transcript. A dimension is the confidence-weighted mean of the ballots that came back and falls back to its static score when none did, so a box with no API key still ranks and the drift between the model and the deterministic floor is reported rather than hidden. The module is itself an Agent Protocol v1 server: create a task with a repo reference and each step runs one voter, with the finished report filed as the task's artifact. Auth is the fleet's — signed tokens from the shared auth module and HMAC session tokens under ~/.mod/reporank/server.secret, against one ACL where reads are open, panel and cache writes need a grant, and the host's owner of record is an owner here too.
